Section 5 (pp.15–19) runs each noisy CWRU inner- and outer-ring signal directly through the SR systems. I checked the abstract, Sections 3–6 and the Data availability statement and found no description of any split unit."},
  "S2_validation": {"code": "C", "quote": "This signal is fed into the two systems, and the optimal parameters are found by GA are as follows:", "location": "p.15", "reason": "There is no ML-style validation set. The GA objective is the output SNR (Section 5.1, step 1), and parameters are optimized on the same noisy bearing signal whose output SNR is then reported in Tables 2–3. That amounts to tuning on the evaluation data, so C is the closest code. This is a best-fit judgment, because the codebook categories assume a train/test design."},
  "S3_checkpoint_rule_code": {"code": "N", "quote": "", "location": "", "reason": "No public code was provided (NO_CODE), and the paper mentions no repository."},
  "S4a_text_discloses": {"code": "Y", "quote": "Determine if the number of iterations has been reached, then output the best individual and end the calculation.", "location": "p.15", "reason": "There are no training epochs or checkpoints. The text does state explicitly that the reported parameters are the best GA individual (by output SNR) after 200 iterations, so the selection rule is disclosed."},
  "S4b_text_matches_code": {"code": "N", "quote": "", "location": "", "reason": "No public code was provided."},
  "S5_runs": {"code": "U", "quote": "", "location": "", "reason": "For the headline bearing results (Tables 2–3, the >3 dB SNR gain), the paper does not say how many GA/simulation runs were performed. The only repetition mentioned is 10 repeats for the simulated anti-noise experiment (Section 4.3, p.13), which is not the headline result. I checked Sections 5.1–5.3 and the table captions."},
  "S5_spread_reported": {"code": "N", "quote": "The output SNR of MDHPSR system is all higher than that of MDCBSR system, with a difference of 3.23 dB between the two at the central end.", "location": "p.16", "reason": "Tables 2 and 3 report single SNR and amplitude values with no standard deviation, interval or other spread measure."},
  "S6_metrics": {"code": "A", "quote": "Table 2 compares the processing effects of the two systems in terms of SNR , output amplitude (A), amplitude gain (AG), amplitude difference ( Δ A ,target amplitude minus maximum interference amplitude), running time (T) and coupling number.", "location": "p.16", "reason": "None of the codebook categories fit. The paper reports no accuracy, confusion matrix, F1, precision or recall; it uses signal metrics only (SNR, amplitude, AG, ΔA, running time). A is the closest code because there is a single family of headline scalar metrics and no class-wise metrics."},
